name: Question 3
problem: Calculate $L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ for the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{{5}^{n}{n}^{n+1}}{(9+5n)^{n}}.$ According to the root test, does ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ converge or diverge?
worked_solution:
Suppose we have the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ such that ${a}_{n}\ge 0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and that $L$ is defined as  

$$
L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n}.
$$

 

Then, the root test states the following:

- If $L<1$, the series converges.

- If $L>1$ or $L=\infty $, the series diverges.

- If $L=1$, the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence ${a}_{n},$ defined as

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{{5}^{n}{n}^{n+1}}{(9+5n)^{n}}.
$$

To apply the root test, we find the limit of $\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{{5}^{n}{n}^{n+1}}{(9+5n)^{n}})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{{5}^{n}{n}^{n}\cdot n}{(9+5n)^{n}})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{5n\sqrt[n]{n}}{9+5n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\sqrt[n]{n}\cdot \frac{5n}{n})}{(\frac{9}{n}+\frac{5n}{n})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{5\sqrt[n]{n}}{(\frac{9}{n}+5)} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 1}{0+5} \\  & =\frac{5}{5} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{n}=1.
$$

Since $L=1,$ the root test gives no conclusion.

html:
Question 3
?

Calculate L=limn→∞ann for the sequence an=5nnn+1(9+5n)n. According to the root test, does ∑n=1∞an converge or diverge?

a
L=19. The series is convergent.
b
L=∞. The series is divergent.
c
L=1. The root test gives no conclusion.
d
L=5. The series is divergent.
e
L=1. The series is divergent.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose we have the series ∑n=1∞an such that an≥0 for all n≥1, and that L is defined as

L=limn→∞ann=limn→∞(an)1/n.

Then, the root test states the following:

  • If L<1, the series converges.

  • If L>1 or L=∞, the series diverges.

  • If L=1, the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence an, defined as

an=5nnn+1(9+5n)n.

To apply the root test, we find the limit of ann as n→∞:

L=limn→∞ann=limn→∞(an)1/n=limn→∞(5nnn+1(9+5n)n)1/n=limn→∞(5nnn⋅n(9+5n)n)1/n=limn→∞5nnn9+5n=limn→∞(nn⋅5nn)(9n+5nn)=limn→∞5nn(9n+5)=5⋅10+5=55=1 Note that we used the fact that

limn→∞nn=1.

Since L=1, the root test gives no conclusion.
